name: H. R. Hygiene Products Limited
identity_note: BSE544848; not R. P. Hygiene LLP. Exact eligible SM master row verified.
summary:
Hold, unresolved. H. R. Hygiene Products Limited has a real manufacturing and distribution business, but its record does not yet establish a reliable, self-funding compounder. The dominant issue is the conversion of reported growth into collectible cash, compounded by a material related-party disclosure inconsistency. FY26 revenue was ₹130.72 crore and PAT ₹11.41 crore, yet three-year operating cash flow was negative ₹6.22 crore against ₹25.15 crore profit. Receivables reached ₹104.76 crore. Growing supplier credit and unpaid tax supported liquidity; these are obligations, not an enduring moat.

BQS, GQS and IAS are all NS, with explicit missing-data bounds rather than invented midpoint scores. GQS means Growth Quality Score. REV cannot be supported as comparable organic growth, CAP lacks attributable incremental-return evidence, R/P lack a supported current funding and valuation basis, and L lacks sufficient verified market history. Financial reliability is on Hold. This is not a finding of fraud or verified default. Management's explanations and the restated auditor's qualification statement are preserved below.

At the 19 October close of ₹59.01, current issued equity is valued at ₹134.02 crore, or 11.75 times FY26 reported earnings. That multiple is not a margin-of-safety conclusion. The conditional base case breaches its required cash floor; its non-rescue IRR and entry price therefore remain null. The optimistic bull simulation yields 34.39% only under aggressive collection improvement and operating assumptions. All ordinary return and entry fields remain null because actual October funding is unverified. Five 1,600-share lots cost ₹472,080, while six cost ₹566,496. This is research, not personalized advice or a trading instruction. [S1][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Exact issuer: H. R. Hygiene Products Limited, BSE SME security 544848, symbol HRHYGIENE, ISIN INE17DP01015. The prospectus traces incorporation to 21 July 2016 and public conversion/name certificate to 10 February 2025. Do not confuse it with related R. P. Hygiene LLP or with larger private hygiene competitors. Research cutoff is 20 October 2026; valuation reference is the 19 October close, not a live executable quote. The five-year nominal INR equity hurdle is 15%, before investor-specific taxes. Financials are standalone Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards; earlier original accounts and later restated accounts are labelled separately.

G1 Conditional: disclosure/control concerns require resolution, but reviewed evidence does not establish a hard integrity failure. G2 Hold: a material related-party purchase-versus-sales conflict, unconfirmed accounts and aged receivables prevent an unqualified financial-reliability assessment. G3 Hold: current cash, bank renewal, IPO deployment and project funding are unverified; conditional funding gaps are not proof of an actual default. G4 Conditional: a 1,600-share lot is verified, while short/incomplete market data and absent order-book evidence prevent implementation certainty. No automatic governance or funding-failure score override is asserted.

Identity and disclosed historical totals have comparatively strong documentary support; economic realizability, incremental returns and current funding have low confidence. The January CRISIL B+/Stable ISSUER NOT COOPERATING rationale concerns insufficient information and dated facilities, not a current solvency certificate. FY22 and FY23 CFO are ND because the retrieved original reports lack cash-flow pages, despite generic auditor wording. H1 FY27 results and current IPO-utilization evidence were not located; no TTM or interim annualization is invented. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S6][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 factor assessments are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV NS, DUR 5, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL 3, EXEC 4, EARN 4, R NS, D 2, P NS and L NS. Every factor below has at least two material facts, contrary evidence, cited support and a confidence assessment. Scores measure the specified evidence, not optimism about a new plant. The selected growth window is FY21–FY26, with FY23–FY26 as a three-year cross-check; the headline rates are shown but not mislabelled as verified organic growth.

Exact Decimal arithmetic gives BQS coverage 0.76, known contribution 2.86 and mathematical missing-data bounds 3.10–5.26. GQS coverage 0.45, known contribution 1.80 and raw bounds 2.35–7.30. Persistent CASH 2 caps the GQS upper bound at 5.00, leaving cap-adjusted bounds 2.35–5.00. IAS has only D known: coverage 0.20, contribution 0.40 and broad mathematical bounds 1.20–8.40. IAS uses final BQS as Q; it does not substitute a midpoint, known-only average or raw bound. These ranges are missing-information arithmetic, not confidence intervals or investment targets.

All three points remain NS. Missing weights are not reallocated, no lower confidence factor can receive a 9–10, and there is no rank based on partial data. G2 Hold independently excludes quality and investment ranking until evidence is reliable; this is separate from the missing factor problem. CASH's GQS cap applies even if future growth evidence becomes available. No GOV≤3 or verified funding-failure IAS≤3 override is applied. [S1][S6][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company manufactures and trades disposable hygiene products, predominantly sanitary napkins, with a Rajkot-area production base and a developing baby-diaper offering. FY26 sanitary products supplied 95.33% of revenue. The company describes its own-brand relaunch after an intentional FY24 slowdown, a catalogue of 25 SKUs, 202 distributors, 25 consignment agents and 99 sales staff. These are issuer descriptions of infrastructure, not independent proof of shelf productivity or consumer loyalty. Offline revenue dominates; online contributes approximately 7.21%.

Economically the business is not simply a branded manufacturer. FY26 manufactured-product revenue of ₹67.22 crore and traded-product revenue of ₹63.50 crore divide the revenue base almost equally. Distribution relationships, credit terms, procurement and collections may therefore matter as much as machine efficiency. A large share of cash is tied up between reported sales and settlement. Largest-customer concentration of 48.35%, top-ten concentration of 80.41% and west-India exposure of 84.4% are more informative than the headline count of 227 customers.

Existing sanitary capacity is 20 crore pieces annually; FY26 production was 18.15 crore pieces. The proposed baby-diaper facility has six crore pieces of capacity and a ₹31.36 crore project budget. New land is leased, not free owned property to add to an enterprise valuation. Rent remains in operating costs; the model does not create an inconsistent lease-debt uplift. The expansion changes execution and working-capital risk before it can be presumed to improve the business mix. [S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Repeat consumption and the social value of affordable hygiene support category demand, but attractive demand is not itself a company moat. Certifications, automated production and local distribution can create entry friction, yet no independently verified market share, sustained price premium, superior unit cost or customer-retention cohort demonstrates durable pricing power. Dependence on one customer for almost half of sales and one supplier for 54.02% of procurement limits bargaining leverage. Polymer, pulp and packaging costs, private labels and established national brands can squeeze margins simultaneously.

Three economic comparators illustrate the gap without importing their valuations. P&G Hygiene and Health Care's FY26 Indian public entity reported ₹4,290.42 crore revenue and ₹856.50 crore PAT, with ₹242.77 crore closing receivables. Its health-care mix, established brands and scale differ materially; its FY25 comparison covers nine months, so a simple raw YoY comparison would be wrong. Nobel Hygiene's dated CRISIL rationale records FY25 revenue ₹765.04 crore, PAT ₹0.23 crore and debtor days of 17, with profitability and credit quality supported by equity infusion and subsidies. It is private and larger, not an automatic benchmark of superior margins. Unicharm offers global technology, brands and India investment access; global parent results cannot substitute for Indian subsidiary economics.

H. R. Hygiene appears smaller and more concentration-dependent, with much slower collections than the cited Nobel debtor metric. Its advantage may be regional distribution and value positioning, but the data does not prove a widening moat. Comparator publication/revision timestamps are not all independently established; their broad business economics are context, not catalysts, price targets or inputs to the issuer's return model. [S1][P1][P2][P3]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Operating revenue grew from ₹22.84 crore in FY21 to ₹130.72 crore in FY26, a five-year reported CAGR of 41.76%. The three-year FY23–FY26 rate is 45.81%; FY24–FY26 is a two-interval CAGR of 24.49%, not a three-year CAGR. Annual additions and rates are embedded in the historical model. A ten-year CAGR is unavailable for this 2016 incorporation; original FY20 comparatives are shown without pretending a full ten-year series exists.

The current trajectory is less impressive than the headline compounding. FY26 total sales grew 14.04%, while manufactured revenue declined 28.02% from ₹93.38 crore to ₹67.22 crore and traded revenue rose 198.92% from ₹21.24 crore to ₹63.50 crore. Production increased only 6.33%, from 17.07 to 18.15 crore pieces. Sales timing, product mix, realized prices, internally manufactured versus purchased goods and inventory movements are not reconciled sufficiently to isolate organic volume-led growth. No acquisition-driven growth was assumed, but that alone does not establish comparability.

The revenue schedule would start at 9 for a verified comparable CAGR above 30%; it is not applied mechanically here because the organic/mix evidence is critical and unresolved. REV is NS, rather than choosing whichever window creates the highest score. The already high existing utilization limits a simple volume-doubling thesis without capacity, outsourced sourcing or lower-value trading. Credible growth confirmation would require a customer/product bridge, sell-through, returns/discounts, subsequent receipts and consistent manufacturing revenue, rather than more distributor registrations. [S1][S2][S3][S4]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The category offers a plausible long runway, but accessible high-return reinvestment is unproven. Baby-diaper sales were only 402,850 pieces and ₹0.3529 crore in FY26. Planned six-crore-piece capacity is about 149 times those sold units, not evidence that such demand is already contracted. At the historical small-volume realization of about ₹8.76 per piece, theoretical full-capacity revenue is only a scale illustration; the actual mix, utilization, wastage, channel margins and pricing may differ. The project must also finance inventory and distributor credit, not merely machinery.

Operating invested capital of ₹70.615 crore is explicitly reconciled to a financing-side identity that retains working capital, operating deposits and unpaid tax/interest classifications. The average-book FY26 post-tax ROIC proxy is 18.99%, while the one-year change in normalized NOPAT divided by capital change is 11.90%. Against an illustrative 14–18% nominal WACC range, the latter is not compelling evidence of value-creating incremental deployment. Neither metric attributes returns to a cohort or project. Comparable three- and five-year incremental operating-capital calculations are ND; CAP remains NS.

The return on new capital therefore cannot be assumed from a headline company ROCE. The model links growth to receivables, inventory, supplier funding, maintenance investment, committed expansion and a retained operating cash floor. Base and bear paths need financing; only the optimistic collection-normalization path is cash-funded on the tested dates. Growth funded by overdue suppliers or tax accrual is not equivalent to self-funded compounding. GQS is capped at 5 because cash realization has been persistently poor, even before resolving the missing REV and CAP factors. [S1]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters' aggregate post-offer holding is disclosed as 48.54%; the remaining 51.46% is not necessarily freely tradable because lock-ins, holder concentration and current restrictions are not verified. Promoter/director loans support funding but remain claims, not permanent common equity. June unsecured debt is ₹9.4105 crore. Prospectus descriptions of demand repayment must be read with lender consent/subordination conditions; unrestricted withdrawal or permanent availability should not be assumed. FY26 director remuneration of ₹0.096 crore is modest relative to PAT, so excessive salary is not the central concern.

The stronger concerns are disclosure consistency and financial controls. The prospectus's related-party table labels ₹15.5588 crore involving R. P. Hygiene LLP as purchases, consistent with another table, while an adjacent explanatory paragraph calls the identical figure sales and 11.9% of revenue. Both statements are retained; no unsupported choice is made about the true direction. Management describes related-party dealings as ordinary course. Receivable and payable balances also involve related entities; independent confirmations, commercial terms and settlement evidence are needed before treating the transactions as clean economic demand.

The auditor chronology matters. A 2023 resignation cited company non-cooperation; 2024 and April2026 changes cited professional preoccupation. The company states changes were not caused by disagreement on qualifications, accounting or internal controls, and reports no material preparation delays over the last three years. The restated auditor reports no qualifications requiring corrective adjustment and relies on earlier auditors for prior periods. These responses are relevant counterevidence, not a reason to erase the non-cooperation history. CRISIL separately retained an issuer-not-cooperating designation. Past compliance and MSME-interest omissions warrant follow-through, but the evidence does not establish diversion or fraud. The project schedule's October orders/November installation/December permits are still prospective at cutoff; failure is not asserted before a deadline. [S1][S6][S7]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The seven-year historical reference separates FY20–FY23 original accounts from FY24–FY26 restated figures, uses the correct source units and retains ND cells. FY22 amounts are in hundreds; FY23 amounts are in thousands. FY21 cash flow was visually checked against its scan and cash roll-forward. FY24/FY25 restated EPS values are reported as disclosed, but exact weighted share counts are not reverse-engineered from rounded EPS. FY26 reported EPS ₹6.41 on the pre-IPO bonus-adjusted basis becomes ₹5.0223 using 22,712,038 issued shares. Bonus changes are not confused with the economic dilution from fresh shares.

FY26 normalized EBITDA is ₹17.0834 crore after excluding other income and retaining non-borrowing finance charges as operating costs; the simpler all-finance-added measure is ₹17.7093 crore. Normalized PAT is ₹10.922925 crore using a 25% tax sensitivity and excluding other income, not a correction to audited PAT. The statutory gross profit is not separately disclosed; revenue less material/purchase/inventory-change costs is only value added before conversion expenses. FY22 PAT exceeds PBT because of tax effects, illustrating why low-base profit CAGR would mislead.

Three-year CFO/PAT is -0.2471 times, with CFO −₹6.2156 crore and cash-capex FCF −₹12.6636 crore. CFO excludes financing-classified interest; subtracting all finance costs gives −₹12.1824 crore. FY26 CFO of ₹1.5779 crore would not exist without large supplier-credit growth and zero cash income-tax payment. Payables rose ₹62.56 crore, while receivables rose ₹55.37 crore and inventory ₹20.34 crore. Closing receivables imply 292.51 sales days; average receivable days are 215.21. The inventory/payable days and 150.99-day cash-cycle proxy have labelled material-cost/purchase denominators, not a claim of exact trade-credit terms.

Receivables at least one year old total ₹33.173 crore, including ₹2.4407 crore older than three years. Management considers the latter good based on assessment, relationships and subsequent collections, but public dated receipts were not provided. Outstanding confirmations and reconciliations remain a limitation even though management expects no material adjustments. Cash/bank ₹1.3709 crore is largely physical cash ₹1.2615 crore; bank cash is only ₹0.1094 crore. The management-verification note differs by ₹0.0001 crore through rounding. Cash-on-hand is not treated as independently bank-confirmed liquidity.

Unpaid MSME interest of ₹0.74 crore accompanies ₹25.8721 crore principal. Earlier interest omissions were corrected in restatement; management says supplier identification occurred at year end and no claims were received. Legacy income-tax provision ₹7.5463 crore and company tax disputes ₹3.8195 crore may overlap. The model pays legacy provision once and tests an additional demand only as an explicitly incremental sensitivity. It does not stack every tax number. Operating property, prepaid costs, restricted deposits and future IPO cash are never added twice. [S1][S2][S3][S4]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹59.01 and 22,712,038 shares, market capitalization is ₹134.023736238 crore. Reported P/E is11.75, normalized P/E12.27 and historical pre-IPO P/B3.16. An intentionally dated diagnostic EV adds June debt ₹23.0662 crore and subtracts only March bank cash ₹0.1094 crore: ₹156.9805 crore, or9.19 times normalized EBITDA. This is not a verified October enterprise value. The IPO is not ignored economically: it appears once in the conditional funding bridge, rather than being presumed to remain free cash in an ordinary valuation.

Fresh proceeds of ₹43.16928 crore, not the ₹10.78528 crore OFS paid to sellers, fund the company. The net expense budget is ₹4.3169 crore; ₹0.4584598 crore already paid before March is credited once against that budget under an explicit offer-cost assumption. There is no duplicate expense deduction or remaining prepaid asset added to value. Project capex ₹31.3612 crore, scheduled loan repayment ₹3.5659 crore, operating capital and legacy claims all consume funding. Current costs and deployment remain unverified.

The model bridges 31 March to 19 October2026 before the investor enters, then models the FY27 remainder, FY28–FY31 and only202/366 of FY32 through19 October2031. Pre-entry profits are not investor distributions; full FY32 cash earnings are not credited. Revenue, margin, tax, working capital, capex, debt, cash floors, shares and terminal claims are linked annually. A2% sales operating-cash floor is retained, not distributed at exit. Rent is an operating expense. There is no new-debt plug, speculative property add-on, warrant cash or repeated IPO proceeds.

Base first breaches its floor in FY27 and peaks at ₹8.7659 crore shortfall; bear peaks at ₹46.8621 crore. Their non-rescue returns and entry prices are null even if cash later improves. Bull conditional IRR is 34.39% and conditional15% hurdle price₹128.61, dependent on collections and execution that are not verified. This is not an ordinary entry recommendation. Separate rescue is described below. Growth×multiple, collection×supplier-credit, bank-only cash, failed rollover, incremental claims, execution-cost and12/15/18% hurdle grids are embedded. The reverse search finds no cash-floor-funded15% solution across0–50% flat growth under the base cash-cycle assumptions; raising growth alone worsens funding.

The DCF tests14/16/18% WACC and3/4/5% terminal growth, reports terminal dependence, deducts cash-floor investment, preserves any signed entry cash deficit and pays legacy claims once. It never adds terminal cash after already valuing explicit free cash flows. Cash-deficient cases retain only labelled financing-agnostic diagnostics, not conditional values or ordinary entry prices. Annual/stub cash balance tests do not establish intraperiod or actual funding adequacy. [S1][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case combines a distributor shock, poor collection of old balances, supplier-credit withdrawal and an expansion that consumes cash before achieving useful utilization. A20% initial sales decline, low margins, slower receivables, excess inventory, reduced supplier credit and15% project overrun are linked assumptions, not independent isolated shocks. Bank renewal and interest-free sponsor support cannot be assumed unlimited. Even with the hypothesized IPO inflow, the path falls below required operating cash. The loss mechanism is impairment of cash claims and dilution, not merely a temporary share-price decline.

The separate rescue simulation issues shares at₹29.505, half the reference price, and pays3% issuance fees. Integer share issuance raises ₹48.31146 crore gross, adds 16,373,992 shares and produces a rescue IRR of -32.51%. The expanded share count is not used in ordinary cases, and the rescue return is not presented as a solvent non-rescue bear return. The assumed availability of buyers is itself uncertain. No forced rights contribution is charged to existing holders while simultaneously diluting them; the model depicts third-party rescue capital.

Legal and contingent exposures require qualification. Nine company tax cases total ₹3.8195 crore, potentially overlapping booked tax. An insurance claim by the company seeks₹0.5 crore after an alleged₹0.6792 crore hailstorm loss; the insurer disputes timing/cooperation and the company denies that characterization. No recovery is credited. The EPCG guarantee of₹0.1063 crore is not assumed payable: management expects fulfilment of export obligations. These disputes do not establish fraud. Permanent-loss risk is High because asset realization, bank funding and per-share claims can all deteriorate together. The central falsifier is whether cash collections and dated funding can cover expansion and existing obligations without fresh rescue. [S1][S6]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold return over five years requires37.97% annual price compounding; tenfold requires58.49%. With unchanged shares, a15-times terminal P/E and8% net margin, fivefold value requires approximately₹558.43 crore sales and tenfold₹1116.86 crore, versus₹130.72 crore now. At a lower10-times multiple, fivefold requires₹837.65 crore. These are algebraic requirements, not forecasts or targets.

The expansion's six-crore-piece diaper capacity does not itself validate that scale. Demand, pricing, channel throughput, capacity utilization and incremental capital returns must all be demonstrated. The present sanitary lines are already highly utilized; substituting low-margin trading could grow revenue without comparable value creation. More receivables at existing terms could increase the funding need faster than the business's own cash generation.

The bull simulation's approximately₹331.17 crore terminal run-rate revenue and14% EBITDA margin are already optimistic. Achieving a five- or tenfold outcome would require an even stronger durable economic bridge, or a speculative terminal multiple, while avoiding dilution. The separate rescue illustrates how expanding enterprise revenue can coexist with destruction of an existing shareholder's claim. Multibagger status is therefore Speculative / unsupported, not a base-case designation. Evidence of genuine brand economics, repeat cash collections and attributable project returns would be necessary before upgrading feasibility. [S1][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The next useful evidence is not another headline growth announcement. First obtain independently reconciled R. P. Hygiene transaction direction, amounts, invoices/terms and settlement, alongside the issuer's explanation of the inconsistent prospectus note. Obtain subsequent collection evidence for aged debtors, bank-confirmed cash, disputed balances and the largest customer's sales/receipts. Compare bad-debt provisions and returns with aging rather than treating management's collectibility assertion as conclusive.

Before considering funding adequacy, reconcile actual IPO receipt, costs, plant payments, debt repayment and remaining restricted/usable funds to a dated bank balance. Verify sanctioned bank limits, utilization, renewal, security, covenants and the terms governing promoter loans. Track booked versus paid tax, MSME principal/interest, and whether any litigation demand is already in provision. A new rating without sufficient information would not close these questions.

For operating validation, compare manufacturing and trading revenue with units, utilization, realizations, customer concentration, credit periods and inventory. Follow the disclosed October order, November installation and December permit milestones without presuming delay before those dates; then require trial production, utilization, yield and cash economics. A positive CFO number caused mainly by further payable stretching is not the same as improvement. Update factor scores only when the missing evidence becomes reliable, retain the cash-quality cap until persistent weakness reverses, and recheck G2 before ranking.

For implementation, obtain complete BSE traded values, zero-trade status, current lot, price bands/surveillance and live depth. Twenty/sixty-session statistics must keep missing observations distinct from zero and pre-listing NA. This is a research checklist, not a scheduled monitoring service, external inquiry or order. [S1][S6][M1][M2][Q1]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold, unresolved; not a demonstrated high-quality compounder, investable growth-at-a-reasonable-price case or supported multibagger. The company has meaningful reported operations and a real proposed capacity expansion, but the financial-reliability and cash-funding issues dominate the apparent earnings multiple. BQS/GQS/IAS remain NS, and G2 Hold prevents ranking. Low confidence is not translated into an invented neutral score or a categorical allegation of wrongdoing.

For a potential new investor, a lower market price does not repair an unverified cash balance, missing project-return attribution or inconsistent related-party disclosure. Conditional bull outputs are only scenario diagnostics. There is no ordinary recommended entry range. For an existing holder, the relevant review is concentration, realizable receivables, funding and dilution exposure; no holding size, cost basis or suitability information is known here. A5-lot position is₹472,080, not exactly₹500,000; the next lot breaches that budget. Short observed trading history cannot guarantee an exit at the quoted close.

The classification could improve with reliable reconciliation, genuine cash collection, dated financing proof and attributable incremental returns. It could worsen if aged receivables require write-offs, suppliers withdraw credit, the expansion absorbs more funds or sponsor/bank support is unavailable. G3 Hold is a verification gap, not a proven default; G1 Conditional is not a hard integrity-failure finding. The evidence supports caution and further verification, not an instruction to trade. [S1][S6][M1][Q1]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The final prospectus and original annual accounts anchor historical data; the rating agency supplies dated credit context, not a substitute for current statements. Exact share claims and the market lot come from an official interoperable security master. Secondary BSE historical OHLCV supplies the reference close and observed volumes; it is not official traded value or a live order book. Official NSE archives supply a session calendar only. Exact upload/revision dates for some issuer index and comparator files cannot be authenticated historically, and they are not used to import post-cutoff events into the forecast. Annual financial values are shown as disclosed, with restatements and unit differences retained.

The substantive unresolved questions are related-party transaction direction; realizability and confirmation of old receivables; current bank cash, renewals and restricted funds; actual IPO costs/deployment; project unit economics and customer commitments; tax-provision overlap and payment timing; current ownership/encumbrances; and complete market liquidity. Forecast sales, margins, tax, cash floor, working capital, capex timing, loan repayment, terminal multiples, rescue terms and DCF rates are explicitly analyst assumptions. Annual solvency tests are not a verification of daily cash availability. All ordinary return/entry fields remain null, as do conditional non-rescue outputs for any cash-floor deficit.

The accompanying source register preserves URLs, hashes, locators and authentication limitations. Private analytical copies exclude raw issuer PDFs, OCR, images and personal identifiers; sanitized facts, calculations and code permit reproducibility, not independent authentication of the underlying originals. Re-download and compare original hashes to authenticate sources. The calculations are a research framework for further judgment, not personalized financial advice, an offer or a trading recommendation. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S6][M1][M2][Q1]

evidence.claim: Exact issuer is H. R. Hygiene Products Limited, BSE SME 544848 / HRHYGIENE / INE17DP01015. Current shares are 22,712,038 and the lot is 1,600.
evidence.locator: Cover, capital chapter and exact-ISIN master.
Original and restated profit-and-loss statements.
evidence.limitation: Manufacturing/trading and price/volume bridge is not reconciled; no organic-CAGR assertion.

evidence.claim: FY26 manufactured revenue fell 28.02% to ₹67.2185 crore while trading nearly tripled to ₹63.5024 crore. Production increased 6.33% to 18.15 crore pieces on 20 crore capacity.
evidence.locator: Business sales and production tables.
evidence.limitation: Sales/production timing and realized-price bridge are unavailable.

evidence.claim: FY26 PAT was ₹11.4066 crore and CFO ₹1.5779 crore. Three-year CFO was negative ₹6.2156 crore versus PAT ₹25.1517 crore; after all finance costs CFO was negative ₹12.1824 crore. FY26 cash income tax was zero.
evidence.locator: Restated profit, cash-flow and tax notes.

evidence.claim: FY26 receivables were ₹104.7599 crore, inventory ₹46.2325 crore and payables ₹95.7042 crore. Receivables at least one year old were ₹33.1730 crore, including ₹2.4407 crore over three years; management considers them good based on assessments and subsequent collections.
evidence.locator: Receivables aging, confirmations and management notes.
evidence.limitation: No dated subsequent-collection evidence was provided; balances awaiting confirmation remain unresolved.

evidence.claim: The ₹15.5588 crore R. P. Hygiene LLP transaction is a PURCHASE in the tables on printed pages 54 and 219, but SALES / 11.9% of revenue in the adjacent page 219 note. Direction is unresolved.
evidence.locator: Printed page 219 / PDF page 223 visually checked; printed page 54 corroborates the table.
evidence.limitation: Direction remains unresolved. Management calls related-party dealings ordinary course; this is not proof of fraud.

evidence.claim: The 2023 auditor resignation cites company non-cooperation; later 2024 and 2026 resignations cite professional preoccupation. The issuer denies disagreements over audit qualifications, accounting or controls and material reporting delay over the last three years.
evidence.locator: Risk factors, printed page 30, and auditor resignation chronology.
evidence.limitation: The restated audit reports no qualifications requiring adjustments; this explanation does not erase the 2023 reason.

evidence.claim: January2026 CRISIL rating is B+/Stable ISSUER NOT COOPERATING. June debt is ₹23.0662 crore: secured ₹13.6557 crore and unsecured ₹9.4105 crore. Cash credit is ₹9.983 crore against a ₹10 crore sanction.
evidence.locator: Debt, printed pages 231–232, and CRA rationale.
evidence.limitation: Dated facilities and ratings do not verify October usable headroom or establish default.

evidence.claim: MSME principal is ₹25.8721 crore and unpaid interest ₹0.7400 crore. Earlier interest omission was restated; management says identification occurred at year end and no supplier claims were received. Legacy tax provision ₹7.5463 crore may overlap company tax disputes ₹3.8195 crore.
evidence.locator: MSME, restatement, tax and litigation notes.
evidence.limitation: Do not stack provisions and demands as independent losses without mapping their overlap.

evidence.claim: Fresh IPO shares of 4,905,600 at ₹88 raise ₹43.16928 crore gross. OFS proceeds ₹10.78528 crore are not company cash. Net budget is ₹38.8524 crore; project ₹31.3612 crore, debt ₹3.5659 crore and general corporate purposes ₹3.9253 crore. Previously paid issue cost ₹0.4584598 crore appears once in the conditional cash bridge.
evidence.locator: Objects, capital and printed page 215 cash share-expense note.
evidence.limitation: Actual costs, timing and deployment after March are unverified. The paid cost relating to this offer is an assumption, not proof of current cash.

evidence.claim: Largest customer contributes 48.35% and top ten 80.41%; the largest supplier accounts for 54.02%. West India contributes 84.4% and sanitary products 95.33% of sales.
evidence.locator: Risk and business concentration tables.

evidence.claim: New diaper capacity is six crore pieces versus 402,850 FY26 pieces sold; capex budget ₹31.3612 crore. October orders, November installation and December permits are prospective milestones.
evidence.locator: Project objects, schedule and product-revenue table.
evidence.limitation: Commissioning and incremental project returns are not verified. Supplier quotations and a management schedule are not contracted sales.

evidence.claim: FY26 normalized EBITDA is ₹17.0834 crore, retaining non-borrowing finance charges in operating costs. Normalized PAT is ₹10.922925 crore at 25% tax. Current-share EPS is ₹5.02227 versus reported ₹6.41.
evidence.locator: Profit, finance, EPS and capital notes.
evidence.limitation: Normalization is an analyst sensitivity. FY24/FY25 weighted shares are ND, not reverse-engineered from rounded EPS.

evidence.claim: Operating invested capital ₹70.615 crore reconciles to the financing identity. FY26 ROIC proxy is 18.99% and one-year incremental proxy 11.90%; attributable cohort returns and comparable three/five-year incremental returns remain unavailable.
evidence.locator: Detailed model capital reconciliation.
evidence.limitation: Average book ROCE cannot replace attributable incremental-return evidence.

evidence.claim: Conditional bear/base paths first breach cash floors in FY27 and peak at gaps of ₹46.86212 / ₹8.76594 crore. Their non-rescue IRR and entry outputs are null. Bull is conditionally funded and yields 34.3905%; all ordinary outputs remain null.
evidence.locator: Annual funding ledger with October entry and terminal dates.

evidence.claim: Separate bear rescue at ₹29.505 per share with 3% fees raises ₹48.31146 crore and adds 16,373,992 shares; rescue IRR is negative 32.5068%.
evidence.locator: Rescue ledger, separate from ordinary and non-rescue returns.

evidence.claim: At ₹59.01, five lots / 8,000 shares cost ₹472,080 and six lots ₹566,496. The 20-session window has 17 observations; the 60-session calendar has 47 observed, five unknown and eight pre-listing NA.
evidence.locator: Exact lot calculations and dated market observations.
evidence.limitation: Short history and unverified traded value/spreads mean L is NS. Missing observations are not zero.

evidence.claim: Prospectus aggregate promoter holding after the offer is 48.54%; public 51.46% is not necessarily unlocked float. Related parties trade with and fund the issuer; director remuneration of ₹0.096 crore is modest against PAT.
evidence.locator: Capital chapter page 80 and related-party notes.
evidence.limitation: Current pledge/ownership and loan repayability require verification; no executable free float is assumed.

evidence.claim: P&G India FY26 revenue is ₹4,290.42 crore, PAT ₹856.50 crore and receivables ₹242.77 crore; FY25 comparator covers nine months. Nobel FY25 revenue is ₹765.04 crore, PAT ₹0.23 crore and debtor days 17, with equity/subsidy support. Unicharm global scope differs materially.
evidence.locator: Primary comparator statements and rating rationales.
evidence.limitation: Periods, scale and scope differ; valuation multiples are not transferred.

evidence.claim: The company claims ₹0.5 crore insurance recovery after alleged ₹0.6792 crore hailstorm damage; the insurer disputes delay/cooperation and the company denies the characterization. EPCG guarantee ₹0.1063 crore is expected by management to be discharged through fulfilment.
evidence.locator: Litigation and contingent-obligation notes.
evidence.limitation: No insurance recovery is booked in valuation and no adjudicated fraud is inferred.
